clue.text: Party time! Partying hard, bit woozy ultimately

indicators.note: letters that go partying are out of order and jumbled about, so the words that follow are rearranged
ultimately points to the very end of the word before it, so only its closing letter is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the final letter of woozy

explanation.surface: A reveller announces it is party time while hitting the drink hard and getting a bit woozy.
explanation.definitionFit: A birthday is the classic occasion for a party, so the day itself is a party time.

clue.text: Printer associates during lockdown with flier

blocks.note: during Covid lockdowns a household could join others in a support bubble
a jet is an aircraft, something that flies

explanation.surface: Someone describes the people they mixed with during lockdown, plus a pilot friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubblejet is a brand name for a type of inkjet printer made by Canon.

clue.text: Once again, came to run a PC without energy

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the other letters wrap around the energy symbol

blocks.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
taken as written
politically correct, in the current slang sense of woke
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone describes running a personal computer that has no power supply.
explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like a personal computer, but it stands for politically correct. E goes in after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: To reawake is to regain consciousness a second time, which is coming to once more.

clue.text: White wine you once overturned? This may be on ice

blocks.note: hock is a German white wine from the Rhine
ye is the archaic form of you

explanation.surface: A glass of white wine knocked over, perhaps, and something left chilling on ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On ice' suggests chilling the wine, but it is ice hockey.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice hockey is a sport played on an ice rink, so this game may well be on ice.

clue.text: Briefly showing the money one gets for a quantity of gas

blocks.note: an airing is a showing, as of a programme or an opinion
the take is the money taken in, the takings

explanation.surface: A show's backer briefly reports how much cash comes in from it.
explanation.definitionFit: An air intake is the amount of air drawn in by an engine or lungs, air being a gas.

clue.text: Hopes to some extent placed in The Times succeeded

indicators.note: something placed in a thing goes inside it, so the next word wraps around

blocks.note: a newspaper refers to itself with the editorial we
the informal suffix ish means to some extent
S abbreviates succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone hopes, more or less, to get something into The Times and does.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times is the newspaper these clues appear in, so it speaks of itself as WE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wishes and hopes are plural nouns, or verbs, for things longed for.

clue.text: Someone who flogs whiskey needing cooler

blocks.note: whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet
hipper means more fashionable, cooler

explanation.surface: A street seller hawking whisky who could do with something to chill it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flogs' suggests selling, but the definition is someone who whips.
explanation.definitionFit: A whipper is a person who beats with a whip, and flogging is beating.

clue.text: European in area south of Nairobi's outskirts poking pig

indicators.note: the outskirts of a place are its edges, so the first and last letters of the city are kept
something poking into another thing pushes inside it

blocks.note: a pig is a slovenly person, a sloven
first and last letters of Nairobi
A abbreviates area

explanation.surface: A traveller in Kenya pokes at a pig on the edge of Nairobi.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue A coming south of NI means it sits below, giving NIA, which goes inside the pig.
explanation.definitionFit: A Slovenian is a native of Slovenia, a country in central Europe.

clue.text: Time engineers put into different film-making location

indicators.note: letters put into a word are placed inside it

blocks.note: else means other, different
T is the abbreviation for time
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Engineers given time on a new film set.
explanation.walkthrough: Elstree is the north London site of famous film studios; the Royal Engineers are a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Elstree Studios, in Hertfordshire, have hosted British film production for a century.

clue.text: Lady, one potentially a queen, we're told

explanation.definitionFit: Bea is a woman's name, short for Beatrice, so it stands for a lady.

clue.text: Caught criminal curious about computing, not going straight

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted out of order
about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go around the next piece

blocks.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
taken as written
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: A crook is caught, with a curious interest in computers, having gone off the straight path.
explanation.definitionFit: A circuitous route goes round about rather than straight to its destination.

clue.text: One old coat for Sophie, tattered? This needs tying up

indicators.note: a coat is the outside layer, so only the outer letters of the name are kept

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
first and last letters of Sophie

explanation.definitionFit: A loose end is an unfinished detail, and one ties up loose ends to finish a matter.

clue.text: Work about empty environment — lines in e.g. Betjeman's Slough

indicators.note: about here means turned about, so the short word for a work is read backwards
an empty word has its insides removed, leaving just its first and last letters

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
first and last letters of environment
RY abbreviates railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: An environmental critique of a town, as in John Betjeman's attack on Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Betjeman's poem Slough begins 'Come friendly bombs and fall on Slough'; Slough is a town west of London. Its lines are poetry, so the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Betjeman's Slough is a poem, so it is an instance of poetry, verse by a Poet Laureate.

clue.text: For Louis I, I'm not sure this shows contempt

explanation.walkthrough: 'Louis I' looks like a king's name; it means the word I as Louis, a Frenchman, says it.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeer is a mocking shout, a display of scorn.

clue.text: Shake and reportedly smash type of fern

explanation.walkthrough: Brake is also an old word for bracken, which is why the fern is spelt that way.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock brake is the parsley fern, a small fern growing among rocks.

clue.text: E.g. daily fun for kids, turning on The Phantom Menace?

blocks.note: a daily is a newspaper published every day

re means on, concerning

explanation.definitionFit: A paper tiger looks threatening but has no real power, an apparent threat that is illusory.

blocks.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union

taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: The Eucharist is the Christian sacrament of Holy Communion, a religious ceremony.

clue.text: Hampers are unopened, firm and small

blocks.note: taken as written
strict means firm, as of discipline

explanation.definitionFit: To hamper is to hinder or limit, so hampers and restricts are matching verbs.

clue.text: Aggression from Uncle Dicky breaking peace

blocks.note: a truce is a peace agreement
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Dicky looks like a name but is the British adjective for shaky.

clue.text: Dreamy, liberal article good for The Scotsman
